newsArticles.summary:
𝐄𝐌𝐄𝐑𝐆𝐄𝐍𝐂𝐘 𝐌𝐄𝐃𝐈𝐂𝐀𝐋 𝐑𝐄𝐒𝐏𝐎𝐍𝐒𝐄 (𝐕𝐄𝐇𝐈𝐂𝐔𝐋𝐀𝐑 𝐀𝐂𝐂𝐈𝐃𝐄𝐍𝐓)
𝐈𝐍 𝐏𝐇𝐎𝐓𝐎𝐒 || Upon arrival at the scene, the responding EMS team found the patient seated on a sofa at the school clinic, conscious and initially alert. The patient reported experiencing a headache accompanied by multiple episodes of loss of consciousness prior to the arrival of the EMS team. An initial assessment was conducted, including evaluation of the patient’s level of consciousness and general condition.
The patient was prepared for transport to the ambulance for further assessment and medical evaluation. Due to the patient’s condition and history of recurrent loss of consciousness, the patient was transferred from the school clinic to the ambulance using a lover’s carry. While being carried toward the ambulance, the patient experienced another episode of loss of consciousness. The responding EMS personnel secured and supported the patient, monitored the patient’s level of consciousness, and continued the transfer to the BFP ambulance.

𝐈𝐍 𝐏𝐇𝐎𝐓𝐎𝐒 || Titay Municipal Fire Station (MFS) Shift A personnel received a report regarding a vehicular accident at Barangay Palomoc, Titay, Zamboanga Sibugay.

Upon receipt of the report, the responding team immediately proceeded to the scene to provide the necessary emergency medical assistance.

Upon arrival, the responding team secured the area and conducted an immediate primary assessment. An adult male patient was found unconscious and unresponsive following the vehicular crash. Initial assessment revealed signs consistent with blunt head trauma, including contusion and swelling around the left orbital area and an avulsion wound on the left frontal region.

Immediate first aid was rendered by applying direct pressure to the frontal wound to help control bleeding, followed by securing the dressing with an elastic bandage. High-flow oxygen was administered via a non-rebreather mask at 15 liters per minute. The patient's condition and vital signs were continuously monitored.

Vital signs were assessed and recorded as follows: BP 100/70 mmHg, PR 70 bpm, RR 20 cpm, SpO₂ 92%, and temperature 36.1°C, with a Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS) score of 5.

Due to the patient's critical condition, he was immediately transported via BFP Ambulance to Dr. George T. Hofer Medical Center, Tenan, Ipil, Zamboanga Sibugay, for definitive medical evaluation and management.

Upon arrival at the medical facility, the patient was safely transferred and properly endorsed to the physician on duty for continuity of care.

TITAY, Zamboanga Sibugay — September 12, 2026 — More than just classroom lessons, fire safety education came alive as the Titay Municipal Fire Station (MFS) conducted a Fire Square Roadshow for student leaders of the Titay District at Titay National High School, Poblacion, Titay, Zamboanga Sibugay. The activity equipped young leaders with essential knowledge and practical skills in fire prevention, basic firefighting, rescue, first aid, and Exit Drill in the Home (EDITH), empowering them to become active advocates of safety and preparedness in their schools, homes, and communities.

The activity aimed to strengthen the knowledge, skills, and preparedness of student leaders in preventing and responding to fire and other emergencies. It provided participants with practical lessons and demonstrations on basic firefighting, rescue techniques, first aid, and Exit Drill in the Home (EDITH).

Adding an interactive approach to fire safety education, BFP Titay also facilitated online fire safety games, allowing participants to test and reinforce their knowledge through engaging and interactive activities.

The Fire Square Roadshow emphasized the important role of students as fire safety advocates and responsible members of the community. By equipping young leaders with essential fire safety knowledge and emergency response skills, the BFP seeks to help build a culture of preparedness and strengthen community resilience.
